Let \(m\geq7\) be an integer and write \([m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Define a finite simplicial complex \(K_m\) on the vertex set \(\{1,2,3,4\}\times[m]\) by declaring that a subset \(F\) is a face precisely when
\[
\left|F\cap(\{i\}\times[m])\right|\leq2\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad
\left|F\cap(\{4\}\times[m])\right|\leq m-5,
\]
and
\[
\left|F\cap(\{1,2,3,4\}\times\{j\})\right|\leq1\quad(j\in[m]).
\]
For integers \(t\geq2\) and \(n\geq2\), let \(M(\mathbb Z/t\mathbb Z,n)\) denote the Moore space obtained from \(S^n\) by attaching one \((n+1)\)-cell along a map \(S^n\to S^n\) of degree \(t\). A wedge identifies chosen basepoints, and a wedge with zero summands is a point.

Determine the homotopy type of the geometric realization \(|K_m|\) for every \(m\geq7\), expressed as a finite wedge of spheres and Moore spaces, with every dimension, cyclic order, and multiplicity given explicitly as a function of \(m\).
</problem>

247	## 4. The incidence quotient and the surviving \(2\)-torsion

249	We need the following integral incidence calculation:

252	M_4[n]/L\cong
253	\mathbb Z^{\binom n4-\binom n2}\oplus\mathbb Z/2,

255	\tag{14}

262	b_A^k=\sum_{\substack{|T|=k\\T\supseteq A}}T,
263	\qquad |A|\le\min(k,n-k),\quad A\text{ ballot},

265	\]

276	\[
277	I_{s,4}(b_A^s)=
278	\binom{4-|A|}{s-|A|}b_A^4.
279	\]

290	\tag{16}
291	\]

321	## 5. The remaining homology rank
322

324	\[
325	R_a=c_a\binom ma\binom{m-a-1}{4-a},
326	\qquad
327	(c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)=(1,3,9,24,54).

330

332	\[
333	b-a_m=\sum_{a=0}^4(-1)^aR_a
334	=\frac{m^4+14m^3-m^2+34m+24}{24}.
335	\]

337	\[
338	b=b_m.
339	\]

341	\[
342	\widetilde H_i(K_m;\mathbb Z)=
343	\begin{cases}
344	\mathbb Z^{a_m}\oplus\mathbb Z/2,&i=m-3,\\
345	\mathbb Z^{b_m},&i=m-2,\\
346	0,&\text{otherwise}.
347	\end{cases}
348	\tag{18}
349	\]

351	## 6. From homology to the homotopy decomposition
352	
353	First, \(K_m\) is simply connected. Let
354	\[
355	J_m=[4]*[4]*\cdots*[4]
356	\]
357	be the join of its \(m\) column sets. This is \((m-2)\)-connected. It has the same \(1\)-skeleton as \(K_m\).
358	
359	Every triangle of \(J_m\) missing from \(K_m\) consists of three vertices in one row of capacity \(2\). Choose a vertex in another row and an unused column. Coning the boundary of the missing triangle to this vertex uses three triangles belonging to \(K_m\). Thus every missing triangular relation already holds in \(\pi_1(K_m)\). Since \(J_m\) is simply connected, so is \(K_m\).
360	
361	Equation (18) and the Hurewicz theorem now imply that \(K_m\) is \((m-4)\)-connected.
362	
363	We use a standard elementary consequence of Hurewicz:
364	
365	> If \(X\) is \((n-1)\)-connected, \(n\ge2\), and its reduced homology is concentrated in degrees \(n,n+1\), then
366	> \[
367	> H_n(X)=\mathbb Z^a\oplus\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z/t_i,\qquad
368	> H_{n+1}(X)=\mathbb Z^b
369	> \]
370	> implies
371	> \[
372	> X\simeq\bigvee^a S^n\vee\bigvee_iM(\mathbb Z/t_i,n)\vee\bigvee^bS^{n+1}.
373	> \]
374	
375	For completeness, Hurewicz gives representatives for the generators of \(H_n\); a representative of order \(t\) extends over the degree-\(t\) Moore space. Sphere representatives for a basis of \(H_{n+1}\), together with the preceding maps, give a homology equivalence from the stated wedge to \(X\). The simply connected homological Whitehead theorem makes it a homotopy equivalence.
376	
377	Apply this with \(n=m-3\ge4\) and (18). This proves the boxed decomposition.
